keywords.def: feel a strong emotion like anger or disagreement
something that makes us determined and enthusiastic
willing to listen to and consider new ideas
a simple solution to a complicated problem

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 大家好，这里是 BBC Learning English 的 6 Minute English。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Beth. Neil, when you're chatting with friends, do you usually have the same or different opinion on things going on in the world?
sentences.zh: 我是 Neil。我是 Beth。Neil，当你和朋友聊天时，对于世界上发生的事情，你们的观点通常是相同还是不同？

sentences.en: Ooh... well, that's interesting. I think I probably have quite similar opinions and that's, kind of, why we're friends.
sentences.zh: 哦……嗯，这很有趣。我想我的观点可能相当一致，这大概也是我们成为朋友的原因。

sentences.en: Ah! Well, we might like to believe that we're accepting and tolerant of others' beliefs, but for many people it can be difficult to communicate with people who have very different opinions to our own.
sentences.zh: 啊！好吧，我们可能愿意相信自己能够接纳并宽容他人的信仰，但对许多人来说，与观点迥异的人交流可能很困难。

sentences.en: And this lack of acceptance could be increasing with our use of social media.
sentences.zh: 这种缺乏包容的情况可能会随着我们对社交媒体的使用而加剧。

sentences.en: For example, algorithms tend to show us what we already like and agree with.
sentences.zh: 例如，算法倾向于向我们展示我们已经喜欢并认同的内容。

sentences.en: Of course, we can't always agree with everyone else.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们不可能总是认同所有人。

sentences.en: We all have personal opinions and beliefs on topics like religion and politics.
sentences.zh: 我们在宗教和政治等话题上都有自己的个人观点和信仰。

sentences.en: But some worry that it's becoming more and more common to react with violence when they disagree, than to solve disagreements together peacefully.
sentences.zh: 但有些人担心，当出现分歧时，诉诸暴力变得越来越普遍，而不是和平地共同解决分歧。

sentences.en: So, are we becoming a more divided society?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们的社会是否正变得更加分裂？

sentences.en: Divided means in disagreement with and separated from others – to not be together.
sentences.zh: Divided 的意思是与他人产生分歧并疏离——不再团结。

sentences.en: And how can we be more accepting and open to the opinions of others?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何变得更加包容，并以开放的心态对待他人的意见呢？

sentences.en: That's what we'll be discussing in this programme and, as usual, we'll be learning some useful new words and phrases.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们将在本期节目中讨论的内容，和往常一样，我们将学习一些有用的新单词和短语。

sentences.en: Remember, you can find all the vocabulary from this programme on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 记住，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到本期节目的所有词汇。

sentences.en: But first I have a question for you, Beth.
sentences.zh: 但首先我有一个问题要问你，Beth。

sentences.en: According to a recent Ipsos poll, what percentage of the British population believes society is divided?
sentences.zh: 根据 Ipsos 最近的一项民意调查，百分之几的英国民众认为社会是分裂的？

sentences.en: I'm going to say 50%. Well, we'll find out the answer later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 我猜是 50%。好，我们稍后将在节目中揭晓答案。

sentences.en: Paul Dolan, professor of behavioural science at the London School of Economics, thinks we should learn how to control our emotions and be open to discussions when we disagree.
sentences.zh: 伦敦政治经济学院的行为科学教授 Paul Dolan 认为，我们应该学会如何控制情绪，并在产生分歧时对讨论持开放态度。

sentences.en: Here, he explains more about how to do this on BBC World Service programme All in the Mind: Generally, we're going to be making better decisions, and more respectfully, if we calm down.
sentences.zh: 在这里，他在 BBC World Service 的节目 All in the Mind 中进一步解释了如何做到这一点：通常情况下，如果我们冷静下来，就能做出更好的决定，并且表现得更尊重他人。

sentences.en: It takes 15 minutes when you're proper aroused for the amygdala to calm down, but within a few seconds it can start calming down, right?
sentences.zh: 当你真正被激怒时，杏仁核需要 15 分钟才能冷静下来，但在几秒钟内它就可以开始平复，对吧？

sentences.en: You take a deep breath and you start feeling calmer.
sentences.zh: 你深吸一口气，就开始感到更平静了。

sentences.en: It's not to say that always being calm is good.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说一直保持冷静就是好事。

sentences.en: Anger can be motivational and positive emotions actually can be very good for us.
sentences.zh: 愤怒可以具有激励作用，而积极的情绪实际上对我们非常有益。

sentences.en: Generally, people make better decisions and are more engaging and more open when they're happier, but much of the time it will be just a case of calming down to try and take some of the heat out of the environment.
sentences.zh: 通常，人们在更快乐时会做出更好的决定，更具亲和力也更开放，但在很多时候，这只是一个冷静下来，试图缓和紧张气氛的问题。

sentences.en: Paul thinks we should take time to calm down when we feel aroused, which here means to feel anger or strong disagreement.
sentences.zh: Paul 认为，当我们感到 aroused（在这里意为感到愤怒或强烈的异议）时，应该花时间冷静下来。

sentences.en: He said it takes 15 minutes for the amygdala, the part of the brain that experiences emotions, to calm down when we're aroused.
sentences.zh: 他说，当我们被激怒时，大脑中感受情绪的部分——杏仁核——需要 15 分钟才能冷静下来。

sentences.en: While anger can be motivational – make us more determined and enthusiastic – Paul says people can speak more openly when they're happier, when heat is taken out of the environment.
sentences.zh: 虽然愤怒可以具有 motivational（激励性）——让我们更坚定、更有热情——但 Paul 说，当人们更快乐、当 heat（紧张气氛）消散时，人们可以更坦诚地交流。

sentences.en: Heat in this context means an intense feeling like anger.
sentences.zh: 在这种语境下，Heat 指的是像愤怒这样的强烈情感。

sentences.en: Now, one recent dating experiment looked into what people say they want in an ideal partner according to their dating profile.
sentences.zh: 最近有一项约会实验调查了人们在约会资料中声称理想伴侣应具备的条件。

sentences.en: Researchers found that many single people included details on things like what they want their partner to look like, their height, the political party they vote for, but many also say they want a partner who is open-minded and tolerant of different views.
sentences.zh: 研究人员发现，许多单身人士详细描述了他们希望伴侣的长相、身高、投票支持的政党等，但许多人也表示，他们希望伴侣是 open-minded（思想开放）且能包容不同观点的。

sentences.en: If you are open-minded, you're willing to listen to and consider new ideas.
sentences.zh: 如果你 open-minded，你就愿意倾听并考虑新的想法。

sentences.en: However, the researchers concluded that while people want a partner to be open-minded and tolerant, they don't want to be very open-minded themselves.
sentences.zh: 然而，研究人员得出的结论是，虽然人们希望伴侣思想开放且宽容，但他们自己却不想表现得非常开放。

sentences.en: So, how can we be more open to getting to know people that we might disagree with?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们该如何更开放地去结识那些我们可能并不认同的人呢？

sentences.en: Here's Paul Dolan again, talking to presenter Claudia Hammond of BBC World Service's All in the Mind.
sentences.zh: 下面再次请出 Paul Dolan，他正在与 BBC World Service 节目 All in the Mind 的主持人 Claudia Hammond 交谈。

sentences.en: So, I guess one very obvious answer is to get offline.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想一个非常显而易见的答案就是离开网络。

sentences.en: I mean, to actually just get out more and meet people because it's what political scientists think is the silver bullet.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，实际上就是多出门见见人，因为这是政治学家认为的 silver bullet（灵丹妙药）。

sentences.en: You know, the more you're around people that are different, the more you realise that actually they're not that different, and you become more tolerant and open-minded.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你接触的不同的人越多，你就越会意识到其实他们并没有那么不同，你也会变得更加宽容和思想开放。

sentences.en: So, being around people that are different – I think that's probably the way that we're going to tackle that problem.
sentences.zh: 所以，多接触不同的人——我认为这可能是我们解决那个问题的方法。

sentences.en: Paul says political scientists think the silver bullet is to get offline and meet people.
sentences.zh: Paul 说，政治学家认为 silver bullet（灵丹妙药）就是离开网络去见人。

sentences.en: A silver bullet means a simple solution to a complicated problem.
sentences.zh: Silver bullet 指的是解决复杂问题的简单方案。

sentences.en: By meeting people who have different opinions and beliefs to you, the more you'll realise they're not that different to you at all.
sentences.zh: 通过结识与你观点和信仰不同的人，你越会发现他们其实和你并没有什么不同。

sentences.en: And that could make you more accepting and lead to a society that is less divided.
sentences.zh: 这能让你变得更加包容，并引导社会减少分裂。

sentences.en: And speaking of divided, isn't it time you revealed the answer to your question, Neil?
sentences.zh: 说到分裂，Neil，是不是该揭晓你那个问题的答案了？

sentences.en: Yes, I asked, "What percentage of the British population believes society is divided, according to a recent poll by the organisation Ipsos?"
sentences.zh: 是的，我问过：“根据 Ipsos 机构最近的一项民意调查，百分之几的英国民众认为社会是分裂的？”

sentences.en: I said 50%. Was that correct? It was not correct.
sentences.zh: 我说是 50%。对吗？不对。

sentences.en: It is in fact 80%. Wow, that's a lot! OK.
sentences.zh: 事实上是 80%。哇，比例很高啊！好。

sentences.en: Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned in this programme, starting with divided, which means in disagreement – not together.
sentences.zh: 让我们回顾一下本期节目中学到的词汇，首先是 divided，意思是产生分歧——不团结。

sentences.en: Aroused means feel a strong emotion like anger.
sentences.zh: Aroused 意思是感受到强烈的情绪，比如愤怒。

sentences.en: If something is motivational, it makes us determined and enthusiastic.
sentences.zh: 如果某件事是 motivational，它会让我们变得坚定且有热情。

sentences.en: Heat means an intense feeling, like anger.
sentences.zh: Heat 意思是一种强烈的情感，比如愤怒。

sentences.en: If you are open-minded, you are willing to listen to and consider new ideas.
sentences.zh: 如果你 open-minded，你就愿意倾听并考虑新的想法。

sentences.en: And finally, a silver bullet means a simple solution to a complicated problem.
sentences.zh: 最后，silver bullet 指的是解决复杂问题的简单方案。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up. If you've enjoyed this programme, why not try practising the new vocabulary you've learnt with our worksheet?
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟时间又到了。如果你喜欢这期节目，为什么不试试用我们的练习单来练习你学到的新词汇呢？

sentences.en: It's available to download now from our website, bbclearningenglish.com, and you could also try out the quiz while you're there.
sentences.zh: 现在可以从我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 下载，你也可以在那里顺便做一下测验。

sentences.en: Goodbye for now. Goodbye!
sentences.zh: 再见。再见！
